name: Flanger sequence pad: triangle plus a pulse one octave up whose level fades out and in once per bar, low-pass, a flanger with its own rate at zero whose delay time is stepped by a square/synced LFO for an arpeggio-like comb movement, then resample pitched down with rising delay/reverb mix for a transition
goal: Make a pad on held chords that moves like an arpeggio without playing extra notes: freeze the flanger's own sweep and step its delay time with a square or saw LFO so the comb peaks jump between positions. Then resample it slowed down into an ambient transition whose delay/reverb mix rises as the sample plays.
prerequisites: Any synth with two oscillators, a low-pass filter, LFOs that can be retriggered or tempo-synced, and a flanger whose rate can be zero (or a modulated short delay with feedback)
Optional vocoder/formant effect and a sampler or audio track for resampling

inputs.name: chords
inputs.description: A looping chord pattern; this is a chord pad, single notes sound thin

inputs.name: tempo
inputs.description: Project tempo for the synced LFOs

outputs.name: transition_fx
outputs.description: Pitched-down resample with rising wet tail

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Keep the flanger's own rate at zero; all movement comes from the stepped delay-time LFO.

Pitch stays steady (Matt's taste): add a few ms of slew on the stepped flanger-time LFO so steps do not click or pitch-glitch, and keep unison detune low and static on the main oscillator. No random pitch modulation.
Resampling down an octave is a deliberate, fixed transposition for transitions, not a wobble.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only pad before that.

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: OscillatorNode + GainNode per layer, BiquadFilterNode (lowpass/highpass/allpass) for filters, DelayNode/ConvolverNode for space, AudioParam automation or slow custom LFOs for movement.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Osc A: triangle with about 3 unison voices and low detune (it plays all the time). Osc B: pulse/square one octave up, level at zero, slightly more voices/detune.
steps.expect: Mellow base with a brighter octave layer ready

steps.action: Put an LFO on osc B's level at a rate of about one bar, retriggered, with a shape that fades out and back in (or drops fast and comes back up slowly).
steps.expect: The octave layer breathes once per bar

steps.action: Low-pass the sound for a mellow tone, with key tracking; filter the harsher upper oscillator more if needed.
steps.expect: Soft pad, upper layer not harsh

steps.action: Add a flanger at full mix (or high), set its own rate to zero, and modulate its delay time (depth/time) with a second LFO: a square wave as an on/off switch, or a tempo-synced 1/8 saw, unipolar, at a small amount. Find a sweet spot by ear, then adjust flanger feedback and phase.
steps.expect: Comb peaks jump between positions, giving arpeggio-like movement on a held chord

steps.action: Optionally add a vocoder/formant effect and adjust bandwidth, formant and band count for color. Lengthen the amp attack and release to remove sharp clicks.
steps.expect: Smoother, more ambient pad with no clicking

steps.action: Record the pad. For a transition, resample it pitched down (slower), place it before a section change, send it to delay and reverb, automate both FX mixes to rise as the sample plays, and fade the sample's level from 0 up to about half.
steps.expect: A swelling transition that ends in pure delay/reverb tail

verification: The flanger's free-running rate is zero; movement stops if the time LFO is disabled.
Osc B's level visibly cycles once per bar.
No audible clicks at the flanger steps.
In the transition, the delay/reverb mix ends higher than it starts, and the tail continues after the sample ends.
